notes: Offensive-line environment profiles. Tiers are 1 (elite) to 5 (league-worst); 3 is neutral and is the assumed default for any team not listed. Every fact is sourced from this repo's own drop pages and Auction Watch corpus (see sourcedFrom), never from memory. Refresh asOf when re-verified.

schema.trend: one of: improved | stable | declined | overhauled
schema.sourcedFrom: repo file(s) the facts came from

DEN.note: Denver graded out No. 1 in offensive-line outlook. An elite line buys the time downfield routes need to develop, and Denver has one of the cleanest offensive-line and schedule combinations for fantasy.
DEN.sourcedFrom: insights drop pages (Denver environment analysis, Waddle trade analysis)

BUF.note: Buffalo pairs Josh Allen with a top-tier offensive line, the two ingredients that most reliably convert a receiver's targets into fantasy points.

NE.note: Top-tier line play supports Drake Maye; his 2025 efficiency profile was not fluky.

MIA.note: Miami projects with one of the league's weakest offensive lines. When protection erodes, offenses shorten their dropbacks and lean run-heavy, and everything downstream gets harder.

CLE.note: The Browns overhauled the offensive line to give the new Monken/Switzer run-action scheme time to function.

LAC.note: An improved offensive line supports Omarion Hampton as the clear lead back under new OC Mike McDaniel.
